title: Introduction to Computer Science: Scientific Programming
description: First course in programming for science and engineering students. Covers variables, control flow, functions, arrays and plotting, using Python to model and analyze scientific data.

title: Introduction to Object-Oriented Programming
description: Problem solving and program design with an object-oriented language. Classes, objects, inheritance, interfaces, recursion and basic testing. Includes a weekly lab.

title: Data Structures
description: Lists, stacks, queues, trees, heaps, hash tables and graphs. Running-time analysis and choosing the right structure for a problem.

title: Object-Oriented Software Design
description: Design patterns, UML, version control and team practices for building medium-sized programs.

title: Computer Organization and Systems
description: How programs run on hardware: data representation, assembly language, memory hierarchy, C programming and the basics of operating systems.

title: Algorithms
description: Design and analysis of algorithms: divide and conquer, greedy methods, dynamic programming, graph algorithms and an introduction to NP-completeness.

title: Software Engineering
description: Theory and practice of building software in teams. Requirements, design, testing, project management and a semester-long client project.

title: Operating Systems
description: Processes, threads, scheduling, synchronization, virtual memory and file systems, with hands-on kernel projects.

title: Human-Computer Interaction
description: User-centered design: needs finding, prototyping, usability testing, accessibility and evaluation of interactive systems. Students redesign a real-world interface.

title: Machine Learning
description: Supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation, regularization, neural networks and responsible use of predictive models.

title: Principles of Software Development
restrictions: Enrollment is limited to Graduate level students.
description: Graduate survey of modern software development: agile processes, testing, continuous integration, code review and maintainable design.

title: Introduction to Machine Learning
restrictions: Enrollment is limited to Graduate level students.
description: Graduate introduction to learning algorithms with a focus on implementation and experimental comparison on real data sets.

title: Introduction to Data Science
description: The data science workflow from question to answer: collecting, cleaning, visualizing and modeling data, and communicating results honestly.

title: Data Visualization
description: Principles of visual perception and design applied to charts, dashboards and interactive graphics.

title: Precalculus
description: Functions and their graphs, polynomial, exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions in preparation for calculus.

title: Calculus I
description: Limits, derivatives and their applications, and an introduction to integration.

title: Calculus II
description: Techniques and applications of integration, sequences, series and parametric curves.

title: Discrete Mathematics
description: Logic, proof techniques, sets, functions, relations, counting, graphs and recurrence relations.

title: Linear Algebra for Engineers and Scientists
description: Systems of linear equations, matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues and applications to data and engineering.

title: Introduction to Statistics
description: Descriptive statistics, probability, sampling distributions, confidence intervals and hypothesis tests, with real-world data.

title: Foundations of Statistics
description: Calculus-based probability, random variables, estimation and inference.

title: General Biology: Information Flow and Evolution
description: Cell structure, genetics, gene expression and the mechanisms of evolution.

title: Principles of Biology I Laboratory
description: Laboratory companion to BIOL 1240. Experimental design, microscopy and molecular techniques.

title: Molecular Cell Biology
description: Membranes, signaling, the cytoskeleton, the cell cycle and the molecular basis of disease.

title: General Chemistry 1
description: Atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, gases and thermochemistry.

title: Organic Chemistry 1
description: Structure, nomenclature, stereochemistry and reactions of organic compounds.

title: Introduction to Philosophy: Self and Reality
description: What is real, what can we know, and who are we? Classic and contemporary answers to the ultimate questions.

title: Ethics
description: Major ethical theories applied to questions of justice, honesty, technology and the common good.

title: Ethics and Technology
description: Privacy, algorithmic bias, automation and work, and the responsibilities of the people who build technology.

title: Theological Foundations
description: An introduction to the study of religion and theology through scripture, tradition and lived experience.

title: Religion and Social Justice
description: How religious traditions have shaped movements for justice, with a required community engagement component.

title: World Religions in Dialogue
description: Comparative study of Hindu, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian and Muslim traditions and the practice of interreligious dialogue.

title: The Art and Craft of Writing
description: Writing as inquiry: drafting, revising and editing essays for different audiences, with attention to research and argument.

title: Introduction to Creative Writing
description: Workshop course in poetry and short fiction. Students read widely and produce a portfolio of revised work.

title: Literature of Migration
description: Novels, memoirs and poetry about crossing borders, belonging and memory.

title: Origins of the Modern World to 1500
description: Connections among the civilizations of Africa, Asia, Europe and the Americas before 1500.

title: St. Louis: A City in History
description: The history of St. Louis from its founding to the present, with site visits and a community history project.

title: General Psychology
description: Survey of the science of behavior and mental processes: perception, learning, memory, development, personality and disorders.

title: Cognitive Psychology
description: Attention, memory, language, problem solving and decision making, with links to the design of everyday things.

title: Principles of Economics
description: Supply and demand, markets, firms, national income, inflation, unemployment and policy.

title: Financial Accounting
description: Preparing and interpreting financial statements: the accounting cycle, assets, liabilities and equity.

title: Public Speaking
description: Researching, organizing and delivering informative and persuasive speeches, with attention to visual aids and listening.

title: Intercultural Communication
description: How culture shapes communication, identity and relationships, and practical skills for working across differences.

title: Elementary Spanish I
description: Beginning Spanish: speaking, listening, reading and writing in everyday contexts, with an introduction to Spanish-speaking cultures.

title: Intermediate Spanish I
description: Review of grammar and expansion of vocabulary through film, news and short readings.

title: Ignite First Year Seminar
restrictions: Enrollment is limited to first-year students.
description: Small seminar for first-year students exploring a big question across disciplines while building habits of inquiry and reflection.

title: Leading Teams and Organizations
restrictions: Enrollment is limited to School for Professional Studies students.
description: Leadership theories, team dynamics, motivation and change management for working adults.

title: Project Management Essentials
restrictions: Enrollment is limited to School for Professional Studies students.
description: Scoping, scheduling, budgeting and risk management for projects of any size.
